## Setup

```{r}
#| label: setting-up-document 


setwd("C:/Users/aay6/Desktop/Blepharisma_Warming/Bleph_warming_Oct_2023_FlowCytometer/All_data")

library(tidyverse)
library(brms)
library(bayesplot)
library(tidybayes)
library(posterior)
library(GGally)

theme_set(theme_classic())
 
df <- read_csv("full_recluster_97p5_filtered.csv")

metric_df_FW <- df %>%
  mutate(
    Algae_Presence = case_when(
      FW %in% c("FW1", "FW2", "FW3", "FW4") ~ "No",
      FW %in% c("FW5", "FW6", "FW7", "FW8") ~ "Yes"
    ),
    number_of_predators = case_when(
      FW %in% c("FW1", "FW5") ~ "2",
      FW %in% c("FW2", "FW3", "FW6", "FW7") ~ "1",
      FW %in% c("FW4", "FW8") ~ "0"
    ),
    ID_of_predators = case_when(
      FW %in% c("FW1", "FW5") ~ "Both",
      FW %in% c("FW3", "FW7") ~ "Blepharisma",
      FW %in% c("FW2", "FW6") ~ "Euplotes",
      FW %in% c("FW4", "FW8") ~ "None"
    )
  )

```

This code calculates the abundance of each cluster within each jar and sampling day while retaining the associated experimental treatment information. It then sums cluster abundances to obtain the total number of events per jar and day and formats key experimental variables for subsequent statistical analyses.

```{r}


# Count number of events per Jar × Day × FW × cluster
cluster_counts <- metric_df_FW %>%
  count(Jar, Day, FW, Temperature,
        Algae_Presence,
        number_of_predators,
        ID_of_predators,
        class,
        name = "abundance")

jar_totals <- cluster_counts |>
  dplyr::group_by(
    Jar, Day, Temperature, FW,
    Algae_Presence,
    number_of_predators,
    ID_of_predators
  ) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    total_abundance = sum(abundance),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
jar_totals <- jar_totals %>%
  mutate(
    Jar = factor(Jar),
    Day = as.numeric(Day),  # keep numeric for trend
    Temperature = factor(Temperature, levels = c("Stable", "Warming", "Recovery"))
  )

jar_totals <- jar_totals %>%
  mutate(
    Algae_Presence = factor(Algae_Presence),
    ID_of_predators = factor(ID_of_predators)
  )

```

```{r}

# Assess overdispersion to inform count-model error distribution
cluster_counts %>%
  group_by(class) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_abundance = mean(abundance),
    var_abundance  = var(abundance)
  ) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = mean_abundance, y = var_abundance)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_y_log10()

```

## Negative Binomial Mixed-effects Model

Model total abundance as a function of temperature, day and their interaction. Jar is included as a random intercept to account for repeated measurements of the same experimental unit through time. A negative binomial likelihood is used to account for overdispersion in the count data.

## Base Model

```{r}

base_abundance <- brms::brm(
  total_abundance ~ Temperature * Day + (1 | Jar),    #accounts for repeated measures/jar specific baseline
  data = jar_totals,
  family = brms::negbinomial(),
  chains = 2,
  cores = 4,
  iter = 3000,
  warmup = 1500,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95),
  seed = 123
)

saveRDS(base_abundance, "base_abundance.rds")

#base_abundance <- readRDS("base_abundance.rds")
```

## LOO Comparisons

```{r}
# Temperature/time can interact separately with predator identity
# and algae presence, but there is no Predator ID x Algae interaction.

fit_bact_id_separate_interactions <- brms::brm(
  total_abundance ~
    Temperature * Day * ID_of_predators +
    Temperature * Day * Algae_Presence +
    (1 | Jar),
  data = jar_totals,
  family = brms::negbinomial(),
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 2000,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.95),
  save_pars = brms::save_pars(all = TRUE),
  seed = 123
)

saveRDS(
  fit_bact_id_separate_interactions,
  "models/fit_bact_id_separate_interactions.rds"
)

# Temperature/time effects can depend jointly on predator identity
# and algae presence.

fit_bact_id_fourway_interaction <- brms::brm(
  total_abundance ~
    Temperature * Day *
    ID_of_predators *
    Algae_Presence +
    (1 | Jar),
  data = jar_totals,
  family = brms::negbinomial(),
  chains = 4,
  cores = 4,
  iter = 4000,
  warmup = 2000,
  control = list(adapt_delta = 0.99),
  save_pars = brms::save_pars(all = TRUE),
  seed = 123
)

saveRDS(
  fit_bact_id_fourway_interaction,
  "models/fit_bact_id_fourway_interaction.rds"
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LOO model comparison
# ------------------------------------------------------------------------------

loo_bact_id_separate_mm <- brms::loo(
  fit_bact_id_separate_interactions,
  moment_match = TRUE
)

loo_bact_id_fourway_mm <- brms::loo(
  fit_bact_id_fourway_interaction,
  moment_match = TRUE
)


# Save LOO results
saveRDS(
  loo_bact_id_separate_mm,
  "models/loo_bact_id_separate_interactions.rds"
)

saveRDS(
  loo_bact_id_fourway_mm,
  "models/loo_bact_id_fourway_interaction.rds"
)

saveRDS(
  loo_bact_id_comparison,
  "models/loo_bact_id_comparison.rds"
)
```

```{r}
loo::pareto_k_table(loo_bact_id_separate_mm)
loo::pareto_k_table(loo_bact_id_fourway_mm)
```

```{r}

  loo::pareto_k_values(
    loo_bact_id_separate_mm

)
```

```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# Exact LOO refits for remaining problematic observations
# ==============================================================================

loo_bact_id_separate_final <- brms::reloo(
  fit_bact_id_separate_interactions,
  loo = loo_bact_id_separate_mm,
  k_threshold = 1
)

loo_bact_id_fourway_final <- brms::reloo(
  fit_bact_id_fourway_interaction,
  loo = loo_bact_id_fourway_mm,
  k_threshold = 1
)
```
